Description: While the piano plays automatically, Oswald and Martha Galley talk about the piece and memories of the past. Afterwards, Oswald decides to go check the room he used to stay in.
Location: Living room (Living room)
Key Information:
  - The dialogue occurs against the background of the piano playing; Oswald and Martha Galley discuss the song and past memories.
  - Oswald says he heard a similar song in childhood and asks Martha Galley for the song’s name.
  - Martha Galley explains the song is an American song and mentions it was purchased by Edmund Galley.
  - As they talk about past memories, Martha Galley says she is glad Oswald came and that the room he used to stay in hasn’t been changed.
  - Oswald decides to go look at the room he used to stay in.
  - Martha Galley reminds him there will be a gathering later and says he can come to her anytime if he needs anything.
  - The conversation is interrupted by thunder outside the window; the piano performance gradually nears its end.
  - After Person No. 3 leaves, there is a knock at the villa’s front door.
Characters:
  [Oswald (Oswald)] Person No. 3, an acquaintance of Martha Galley who once lived here.
    · Discusses the piano piece with Martha Galley and reminisces about the past.
    · Asks Martha Galley the name of the song and says the lyrics are interesting.
    · Decides to go look at the room he used to stay in.
    · Says he doesn’t want to see the other guests and prefers being alone.
  [Martha Galley (Martha Galley)] Person No. 5, the female owner of the villa.
    · Reminisces with Oswald and discusses the piano piece.
    · Explains the piano was bought by Edmund Galley and says Oswald likes the song.
    · Reminds Oswald there will be a gathering later and tells him he can come to her if he needs any help.
